title: Biological Applications of Emergent Information Processing: Fast, Long-Range Synchronization
content: The main objective of this research is twofold: (a) to demonstratethat life can be understood as a continuous flow of micro-processes that are operating above a constituting matrix (medium), and (b) provide a specific example of this flow in the form of a long-range coordination within short-range communicating medium. Those goals are achieved by the application of the concept of emergent information processing that utilizes uniform changes of the applied neighborhood to all updated elements of the matrix. A very fast solution to a generalized, long-standing, generic computational problem dealing with long-range synchronization within massively-parallel, short-range communicating environments (similar to one-dimensional cellular automaton known under the name firing-squad synchronization problem) is presented: it is called the semi-two-dimensional synchronization problem (S2D-SP). The number of steps ts, which is necessary to synchronize a cell array, is substantially lower than the width of the synchronized cell array w, i.e., ts < w. In addition to the pure theoretical importance, the solution demonstrates the usefulness of the concept of extended neighborhoods in search of biologically relevant computational models of self-organization and emergence. The presented solution to the modified FSSP problem is uncovering a novel road towards the design of artificial emergent systems and paving a path towards understanding of natural computation.
